style: set the scene in one or two plain sentences

candidates.evidence: मत्तः (from me) / सर्वम् (everything) / प्रवर्तते (proceeds, moves forth)

candidates.angle: the wise worship with wholehearted devotion
candidates.evidence: बुधाः (the wise) / भावसमन्विताः (endowed with devotion, feeling, wholeheartedness)

angle_hi: मत्तः: मुझसे ही सब कुछ प्रवृत्त होता है

en.intro: Krishna has shown his many forms. Now he says where they all come from. Listen to who moves and what the wise do.
en.notice: Notice the word matatah, from me. Everything that exists, Krishna says, moves and proceeds from him.
en.next: The wise, knowing this, worship me with wholehearted devotion.
en.meaning: I am the source of all; everything moves from me. Knowing this, the wise worship me with wholehearted devotion.

hi.meaning: मैं संसारमात्रका प्रभव मूलकारण हूँ, और मुझसे ही सारा संसार प्रवृत्त हो रहा है अर्थात् चेष्टा कर रहा है ऐसा मेरेको मानकर मेरेमें ही श्रद्धाप्रेम रखते हुए बुद्धिमान् भक्त मेरा ही भजन करते हैं सब प्रकारसे मेरे ही शरण होते हैं
hi.notice: मत्तः शब्द पर ध्यान दीजिए, अर्थात् मुझसे। कृष्ण कहते हैं कि सब कुछ मुझसे ही प्रवृत्त होता है, चलता है।
hi.next: बुद्धिमान् भक्त यह जानकर मेरी ही शरण में रहते हैं और भावसमन्वित होकर मेरा भजन करते हैं।

issues: meaning_changed: "सुनिए, कौन चलता है और कौन ठहरता है" (This phrase in the Hindi intro ('who walks and who stays') is not in the source or the known Mahabharata story. It adds an unsupported narrative detail about 'staying' that contradicts the verse's meaning, which focuses on the source of all and proceeding from the speaker.)

contrast_template: "केवल पूजा नहीं करते, बल्कि भावसमन्वित होकर" (The Hindi notice/next verse uses 'बल्कि' (but), implying a contrast ('not merely worship, but...'), which is not present in the original Sanskrit 'भावसमन्विताः' (endowed with devotion). The original does not contrast worship with resting; it describes the manner of worship.)

borrowed: "notice: 'Everything that exists, Krishna says, moves and proceeds from him, yet he remains the source of all.'" (The phrase 'yet he remains the source of all' is not present in the source verse (10.8) nor in the NEXT verse (10.9). It seems to be a general commentary or an addition not supported by the text, making it a borrowed/unsupported insertion.)
